detailed_findings.finding: The exponent computation is correct and complete: multiplicities are counted as the difference between numbers of multiples of t in two intervals, then rewritten as floor differences.

The converse polynomiality argument is valid: a negative cyclotomic exponent produces a nonconstant denominator factor that cannot cancel with the numerator because distinct cyclotomic polynomials are pairwise coprime.

reason: The proof establishes the cyclotomic exponent formula by counting, via the standard factorization q^N - 1 = product_{r|N} Phi_r(q), and converts those counts to the stated floor expressions. It then proves the polynomiality criterion in both directions: nonnegative exponents give a finite product in Z[q], while any negative exponent yields a nontrivial denominator factor that cannot cancel because distinct cyclotomic polynomials are pairwise coprime. The argument matches the lemma sketch and supports the stated role in the assembly.
